evidence.claim: Article 104 vests executive authority in the President, including national-security policy, treaty ratification, appointment and dismissal of ministers and senior officials, military-use decisions, and presidential decrees subject to legal limits; Article 116 lets the TBMM or the President renew elections; Article 105 sets a parliamentary investigation path.
evidence.title: Anayasa | Anayasa Mahkemesi
evidence.excerpt: Article 104 vests executive authority in the President, including national-security policy, treaty ratification, appointment and dismissal of ministers and senior officials, military-use decisions, and presidential decrees subject to legal limits; Article 116 lets the TBMM or the President renew elections; Article 105 sets a parliamentary investigation path.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary constitutional text governing the 2022 presidency; direct and stable legal authority/constraint source.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Defines Erdoğan's office-level authority and checks in 2022; not a claim about personal conduct.
contrary_evidence: The same articles constrain decree power and preserve parliamentary/judicial checks.
Formal authority does not prove how he used it in practice.

evidence.claim: Police violently broke up the student-organized Pride march at Middle East Technical University in Ankara on 10 June, detaining 37 students after dragging some of them on the ground.
evidence.title: Türkiye: Further information: Pride march dispersed with excessive force
evidence.excerpt: Police violently broke up the student-organized Pride march at Middle East Technical University in Ankara on 10 June, detaining 37 students after dragging some of them on the ground.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous human-rights reporting on a specific event with a clear date and casualty/detention count.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The conduct is attributed to Turkish police and the authorities allowing the crackdown; it does not show a presidential order by itself.
contrary_evidence: Authorities framed the event as a public-order issue.
The incident is a specific protest crackdown, not proof of nationwide mass terror.

evidence.claim: Erdogan said a constitutional amendment would protect families from what he called 'perverse trends' and said he wanted to 'protect the family establishment' against LGBT-related change.
evidence.title: Erdogan says constitutional change will protect families against 'perverse trends'
evidence.excerpt: Erdogan said a constitutional amendment would protect families from what he called 'perverse trends' and said he wanted to 'protect the family establishment' against LGBT-related change.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on a direct Erdoğan quotation; useful for ruler attribution even though republished by Yahoo.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct personal attribution to Erdoğan, not merely to subordinates or local police.
contrary_evidence: The speech was framed as family-protection politics by Erdoğan and AKP supporters.
It is rhetoric, not proof of a specific violent act.

evidence.claim: A Turkish court sentenced Istanbul Mayor Ekrem Imamoglu to jail and imposed a political ban on the opposition politician seen as a strong challenger to President Tayyip Erdogan.
evidence.title: Turkish court sentences Erdogan rival to jail with political ban
evidence.excerpt: A Turkish court sentenced Istanbul Mayor Ekrem Imamoglu to jail and imposed a political ban on the opposition politician seen as a strong challenger to President Tayyip Erdogan.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters event reporting with direct political consequence and a clear date.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The court action was not personally ordered by Erdoğan in the source, but it is relevant to the political-fear environment under his rule.
contrary_evidence: The judgment was subject to appeal.
This is political punishment rather than direct physical violence.

evidence.claim: In April 2022 the Turkish Parliament adopted an AKP-MHP proposal that lowered the electoral threshold from 10 percent to 7 percent and changed the selection of provincial and district election boards through a lottery, which the report says may endanger election security.
evidence.title: Türkiye 2022 Report
evidence.excerpt: In April 2022 the Turkish Parliament adopted an AKP-MHP proposal that lowered the electoral threshold from 10 percent to 7 percent and changed the selection of provincial and district election boards through a lottery, which the report says may endanger election security.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary EU report summarizing the new electoral-law design and its risks.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Erdoğan's governing coalition; it reflects ruler-era rule design rather than local administrative drift.
contrary_evidence: The report also notes the threshold reduction was a positive development in representation terms.
The law did not by itself cancel competitive elections.

evidence.claim: Independent Turkish media faced significant pressure in 2022, with government organisations advertising almost exclusively in pro-government outlets, critical outlets repeatedly fined by RTÜK, and online news sometimes blocked or ordered removed by courts.
evidence.title: Turkey
evidence.publisher: Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism
evidence.excerpt: Independent Turkish media faced significant pressure in 2022, with government organisations advertising almost exclusively in pro-government outlets, critical outlets repeatedly fined by RTÜK, and online news sometimes blocked or ordered removed by courts.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: University-based annual media report published contemporaneously, synthesizing newsroom and market conditions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Describes the media environment under Erdoğan's government; the fines and blocks were executed by regulators and courts.
contrary_evidence: The report also notes independent outlets continued to reach audiences through social platforms.
It is descriptive rather than a formal legal finding of censorship intent.

evidence.claim: RSF said 90 percent of national media were under government control and that Turkey ranked 149th out of 180 in RSF's 2022 World Press Freedom Index.
evidence.title: RSF unveils 15-point press freedom plan for Turkey, five weeks before elections
evidence.excerpt: RSF said 90 percent of national media were under government control and that Turkey ranked 149th out of 180 in RSF's 2022 World Press Freedom Index.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specialist press-freedom monitor summarizing the state of the media system and its 2022 ranking.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective, but explicitly anchored to the 2022 index and the pre-election media environment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributes the control environment to Erdoğan-era political patronage and institutional capture.
contrary_evidence: This is advocacy-oriented and intentionally forceful in tone.
It is a system-level assessment, not a case file.

evidence.claim: A Turkish court imprisoned pending trial 16 Kurdish journalists and media workers after they had been kept in custody for eight days without being formally accused, on propaganda charges tied to terrorism allegations.
evidence.title: Turkey jails 16 Kurdish journalists over propaganda charges
evidence.excerpt: A Turkish court imprisoned pending trial 16 Kurdish journalists and media workers after they had been kept in custody for eight days without being formally accused, on propaganda charges tied to terrorism allegations.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters dispatch with precise date, counts, and detention details reproduced by Euronews.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to Turkish police, prosecutors, and courts operating under Erdoğan's government; not framed as a presidential order.
contrary_evidence: Authorities treated the case as anti-terror enforcement.
The article is press-freedom focused and not a broad governance survey.

unresolved_gaps: Direct 2022 nuclear-specific conduct is sparse; most positive evidence is alliance or humanitarian diplomacy rather than nuclear command, doctrine, or safety reform.
The package shows limited exposure and inherited NATO structure, but not a strong ruler-attributed improvement or deterioration in nuclear posture.

The package is strong on mediation and selective coercion, but weaker on independent verification of the civilian-harm allegations and on Erdoğan's own weighing of peaceful alternatives for the Syria/Iraq operations.
Several items are civic-space or press-repression evidence rather than direct physical-integrity harm, so the chapter partly relies on fear-climate inference.
Attribution for some harms is institutional rather than command-specific, especially for local policing and court actions.
There was no true 2022 succession or term-limit stress test, so the chapter relies on institutional erosion and media/election-law evidence instead of a direct transfer-of-power event.
Outcomes are heavily confounded by inflation shocks, external demand, the post-pandemic rebound, and CBRT formal independence, so causal credit remains partial.
Project-level delivery and regional/household distribution evidence are thinner than macro indicators.
The strongest welfare evidence is on health coverage and refugee cash transfers; housing, sanitation, and school-quality evidence is thinner.
Several positive items are donor-UNICEF/WHO partnerships, so Erdoğan attribution is meaningful but not exclusive.
There is no direct 2022 audited asset, gift, or procurement record for Erdoğan personally.
The strongest negative items are media-control and family-network allegations, not direct first-person dishonesty or self-dealing proof.
Project-level completion evidence is thin; the package shows allocation, program design, and some outcomes, but not audited delivery for specific 2022 initiatives.
Outcome attribution is still confounded by shocks and by private-sector behavior, especially on growth, exports, and labor-market statistics.
